response.answer: David Hockney's exhibition "David Hockney: Portraits in Print" is on display at the National Gallery of Australia from September 5, 2026, to May 9, 2027. The exhibition highlights Hockney's early works and his experiences as a gay man finding his identity. The National Gallery of Australia holds one of the most significant collections of Hockney's works in the Southern Hemisphere. Additionally, the National Gallery, London, will host a tour titled "David Hockney through the collection: A lifelong source of inspiration" on November 18, 2026, exploring Hockney's inspirations from the gallery's collection.

### About [...] The technological experimentation that characterised Hockney’s 50-year career, from Polaroids to photocopiers and iPads was nonetheless inspired by the greats of art history and especially those in the National Gallery collection.

Join us on a tour of the collection from the first image which inspired Hockney in his childhood home, the works which he incorporated into his own pieces and his later versions of famous work which allowed him to explore his own groundbreaking ideas on perspective.

Overlooked in that canon is a stranger, more private painting: _Beverly Hills Housewife_, a 12-foot portrait that Hockney painted between 1966 and ’67. A new book by critic and curator James Cahill, out in the U.K. now and in the U.S. on November 3, argues the painting captures the artist’s new, “crystalline realist” style, and ultimately reveals two people—the artist and the subject—caught in a moment of transformation.
